title: Reversibility/saturation condition and Delta F = 0 for binary ratchet unproven (Thm 4, Cor 3)

comments.author: human
comments.body:
The solution invokes the generalized second law as a framework hypothesis (acceptable), but then repeatedly uses its **equality (reversibility) condition** (Thm 4 `thm:work`, Cor 3 `cor:eff`, Prop 1) without (i) stating the precise reversibility/saturation criterion, and (ii) verifying it can hold for a **binary, irreversible switching** ratchet. Quasi-static binary flashing is generally NOT reversible: switching ON/OFF at finite particle density dissipates relaxation heat. The existence of a reversible binary protocol attaining $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle=k_BT I_A$ is asserted, not established (ties to the trade-off gap).

Additionally, 'cyclic/steady operation gives $\Delta F=0$' (eq. `workbound-cyclic`) is asserted without definition. In a feedback NESS the particle distribution is not canonical, so $F=-k_BT\log\int_0^L e^{-V/k_BT}$ (the ON-equilibrium free energy) is not obviously the relevant $F$. The nonequilibrium free-energy bookkeeping ($F[\rho]=\langle V\rangle_\rho-k_BT S[\rho]$, Esposito--Van den Broeck) and a proof that $\Delta F=0$ over a period are needed.
